page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU with 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included in this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3957.38 and a gzip compression rate of 43.72 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is strong, scoring 63342.27 in stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory performance is mixed; large-block read-only memory bandwidth is strong at 223.85 GB/sec, while write bandwidth and small-block read bandwidth remain in the average tier. For AI workloads, the NVIDIA L4 GPU achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 339.34 tokens per second on a small 135M LLM model, alongside average prompt processing speeds.

Given the shared CPU allocation and lack of bundled local storage, this instance offers a specialized hardware profile that balances high-capacity system memory and dedicated GPU resources. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require substantial GPU acceleration and large memory footprints without needing dedicated CPU cores or local NVMe drives. Recommended workloads include machine learning inference, data science tasks, graphics rendering, and memory-intensive GPU-accelerated applications.

Operating on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, this instance lacks local storage but offers a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. Benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core capabilities, alongside top-tier text generation speeds of 339.34 tokens per second for small language models. Large-block memory read bandwidth is strong, while write bandwidth and database operations perform at average levels. This configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive GPU workloads, machine learning inference, and data science applications that do not require dedicated CPU allocations or local storage.
